Agronomist, member of the Ordre des agronomes du Québec. 15 years of experience in agri-environmental work and agricultural regulation in Quebec.

---

## Agricultural potential and CPTAQ applications

An application to the Commission de protection du territoire agricole du Québec (CPTAQ) — subdivision, transfer, rezoning, resource extraction — rests largely on the agricultural potential of the lot in question.

I establish this diagnostic and support the filing of the application with the Commission.

**Who this is for**: landowners, developers, municipalities, and MRCs.

---

## Pre-purchase or pre-lease diagnostic

Knowing a piece of land's real potential before buying or leasing it avoids unpleasant surprises. A voluntary diagnostic, with no regulatory process attached.

**Who this is for**: buyers, tenants, and investors in farmland.

---

## Water and soil health diagnostic

Recurring excess water, underperforming zones, soil structural condition: a diagnostic established before a site visit even happens.

Potentially eligible for financial support under the Programme services-conseils.

**Who this is for**: farmers in active operation.

---

## PAEF and PAA

Agri-environmental fertilization plan (PAEF) and agri-environmental support plan (PAA) — two services I practiced for several years before specializing in geospatial data.

Potentially eligible for financial support under the Programme services-conseils.

**Who this is for**: farmers in active operation.

---

## Scope of my services

I do not carry out wetland delineation (a botanical expertise I don't hold).

My diagnostics don't replace a subsurface drainage system design plan, which falls under engineering. They support an agronomic decision — understanding where and why water behaves a certain way in a field — not the technical design of the network.

The limits specific to each data source (LiDAR, soil maps, satellite imagery) are explained at the time of the diagnostic, not buried in fine print.
